notes: Checked: full mega-menu (Uitgelicht/Featured section incl. 'Nieuw' dropdown with Woontrends sub-collections, Woonaccessoires, Meubels, Herfstdecoratie, Geurlijn), footer nav ('Populaire categorieen' = category list, not a bestsellers link), site search for 'bestseller' (319 hits, but spot-checked names are unrelated everyday items -- mugs, cutting boards, wine glasses -- confirming the search engine does broad fuzzy text matching rather than surfacing a real bestsellers concept; a nonsense query returned 0 hits so the engine is not flat-default, it is just noisy on this term), and slug probes (/best-sellers, /bestverkocht, /topverkocht, /meestverkocht, /meestverkochte-producten, /populaire-producten, /favorieten, /top-sellers all 404). No page or nav item literally labelled Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Meest Verkocht/Populair exists. The one candidate found: a 'Trending' tile inside the /nieuw page's category-slider (sibling to Woontrend collections), resolving to https://www.xenos.nl/trending, a genuine catalog PLP (H1 'Trending', total_items 59, page_size 48, last_page 2, ceil(59/48)=2 matches). Its own meta description reads 'Trending - iedere week nieuwe en trending items' (weekly new + trending items) and intro copy is 'Ontdek de nieuwste trends en must-haves van Xenos' (discover the newest trends and must-haves) -- language of style/seasonal trend curation, not sales-rank popularity. Spot-checked product names show a stylistically coherent beige/brown palette selection (side tables, fluffy chairs, lamps) typical of a curated trend edit rather than a randomly-mixed top-sellers list. Because 'Trending Products' is one of the brief's own listed target terms and this cannot be confidently placed on either side of the trend-vs-popularity line, it is recorded here with a manual-review flag rather than silently dropped or silently kept.
